item.title: Hair products laced with cancer-causing chemicals would come with a warning label under new Colorado bill
item.description: A growing body of research shows hair relaxers, straighteners and synthetic hair frequently used by Black women are associated with higher cancer risks

item.title: Bill to protect Colorado workers from extreme weather gets another try
item.description: Climate change presses need for shade, clean water, winter warmups and more for vulnerable employees, backers say

item.title: It’s up to Colorado to shield consumers from the price shock of Xcel Energy’s data-center related building boom
item.description: Colorado utilities regulators have a tall order: cut pollution, promote electrification and economic development while slowing rise of electric bills

item.description: Plus: Two whimsical fiber art installations and a visit from the American Ballet Theatre

item.title: Broomfield measles outbreak now up to as many as 10 cases

item.title: “What’d I Miss?”: Is Norway the right way?
item.description: In "What'd I Miss?" Myra discusses the way one nation uses taxes to help alleviate a problem that besets many Americans — student and health care debt.

item.title: Jim Morrissey: Will a “TP” legacy stick to Polis?
item.description: Cartoonist Jim Morrissey imagines that if Gov. Jared Polis lets election denier Tina Peters out of prison early, the repercussions could be hard to shake.

item.title: Drew Litton: Are Broncos turning a blind eye to NFL free agency?
item.description: Cartoonist Drew Litton wonders if the Denver Broncos really think they can progress toward the Super Bowl without going shopping for some upgrades.

item.title: As violent crimes spike on the Ute Mountain Ute Reservation, support from the federal government is lacking
item.description: Tribal leaders say 10 Bureau of Indian Affairs law enforcement officers were assigned to the reservation to curb violence. Sens. Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper, along with Rep. Jeff Hurd, are asking why they only have one.
